title: The confident lie
system: You are a coding agent. Use the tools to change files and run tests. Say done when the work is finished.

script.say: The text_utils module has a word_count helper. Using it.

tools.new_text:
from text_utils import word_count
    return word_count(s)

then.say: The check failed. Running the tests to see why.
This project has no text_utils module. Counting the words directly.

tools.old_text:
from text_utils import word_count
    return word_count(s)

incident.why: The model says all tests pass, and it never ran them. Its reply is fluent and sure, and it names a helper that this project does not have. Nothing checks the claim, so the harness takes it as done and ends the run.
incident.hint: Find the first name the model relies on. Does this project have it?

notes.text: That reply names a helper this project does not have. Models make mistakes like this all the time. The failure comes later: when does anything check the claim?

fixes.text: Run the tests on every done claim, and send a failure back to the model
fixes.why: A fluent claim becomes a question the harness answers. A failure goes back to the model, which fixes it.

fixes.text: Ask the model to check its own work before it says done
fixes.why: It may catch the mistake, but that check is more of its own words. Only a run shows what is true.

fixes.text: Use a model that does not make things up
fixes.why: No model is immune to a confident wrong answer. The check belongs in the harness.
